input.question: How did O.J. Simpson win the trial of the century?
input.ground_truth: The evidence was all circumstantial. They couldn't place him at the scene, it all pointed at him but none of it was conclusive. The one thing they did have was some blood that was sure win except DNA evidence was largely new at the time so the lawyers were able to convince the jury that it was mishandled and couldn't be accurate. Also they played the race card hard. They made it look like it was the white system just looking for another guilty black man. In the end its truly messed up because the book he wrote is essentially a confession and how to get away with murder for dummies.

Question: How did O.J. Simpson win the trial of the century?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine there was a big, famous case, like a giant puzzle, and everyone in the country was watching. The puzzle was about whether O.J. Simpson did something very, very bad. Lawyers on both sides tried really hard to show what really happened. The people who decide (called the jury) listened to everything and then had to choose if O.J. did it or not. In the end, they decided he did **not** do it, so he didn’t get in trouble. That’s why people called it the “trial of the century”—because it was so big and everyone was talking about it!
